mutants.why: APFS containers are keyed by the exact ASCII 'NXSB'; probing for 'NXSC' leaves a real NXSB image undetected and the detector falls through to std::nullopt. detectsApfsContainerByNxsbMagic asserts detection.has_value() and file_system == "APFS"

the NXSB magic lives at container byte 0x20; probing 0x21 reads 'XSB' + a stray byte and matches nothing, so the APFS image is missed. detectsApfsContainerByNxsbMagic asserts file_system == "APFS" for a buffer with 'NXSB' written at 0x20

shortening the magic compare to 3 bytes accepts any buffer beginning 'NXS', so a corrupt 'NXSX' superblock is misreported as APFS instead of failing closed. rejectsApfsWhenFourthMagicByteWrong writes 'NXSX' at 0x20 and asserts !detection.has_value() -- the full 4-byte compare is required to reject it

the family label routes which reader runs; emitting 'APFSX' mislabels every APFS container. detectsApfsContainerByNxsbMagic asserts file_system == "APFS" exactly, not merely non-empty (so the fuzz slot's non-empty check would miss this)

a boot sector with the 'NTFS    ' OEM tag must report NTFS, not exFAT; the wrong family routes the wrong reader at a matching boot signature. detectsNtfsBySignedBootSectorOemTag asserts file_system == "NTFS"

the NTFS OEM signature is the literal 'NTFS    '; corrupting the first byte makes a real NTFS boot sector match no Windows family, so detectBytes falls through to std::nullopt. detectsNtfsBySignedBootSectorOemTag asserts detection.has_value() and file_system == "NTFS"

the ext superblock magic 0xEF53 sits at superblock offset 0x38 (image byte 0x438); shifting to 0x39 reads the high magic byte 0xEF where 0x53 is expected, so hasExtMagic fails and the image is missed. detectsExt2ByEf53SuperblockMagic asserts file_system == "ext2"

the ext magic little-endian low byte is 0x53; requiring 0x54 makes hasExtMagic reject every genuine ext superblock. detectsExt2ByEf53SuperblockMagic writes 0xEF53 at 0x438 and asserts file_system == "ext2"

a superblock with no journal/64bit/extent/ro-compat feature flags is ext2; the default branch must not claim ext4. detectsExt2ByEf53SuperblockMagic uses an all-zero-feature superblock and asserts file_system == "ext2"

the 'H+' volume-header signature is HFS+, distinct from the 'HX' case that yields HFSX; swapping the branch label misroutes HFS+ volumes. detectsHfsPlusByVolumeHeaderSignature writes 'H+' at 1024 and asserts file_system == "HFS+"

inverting the no-data guard makes every NON-empty buffer take the fail-closed std::nullopt path immediately, so no real signature is ever examined. detectsApfsContainerByNxsbMagic (and every other positive case) asserts detection.has_value() on a non-empty image and now receives std::nullopt
